text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- It is the week for Cyprus next week at the United Nations. A meeting of the permanent five and special representatives of foreign governments are scheduled to take place on the Cyprus issue.
- The Security Council is expected to discuss Cyprus next week.
- Some 32,000 sheep face the chop for the Easter feast.
- Women remain scarce in the top paid jobs. One in five men are in the top income bracket compared to one in twelve women.
- Developments on the Cyprus issue are now focused in New York.
- Nothing new has emerged in the positions of the two sides in the proximity talks, but the United Nations will still call direct talks in the first half of the year.
- Two out of three students take extra tutorial lessons.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash provokes and blackmails. He is laying down terms for the recognition of the pseudo-state from pilgrims due to visit the Apostolos Andreas monastery for Easter.
